turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me, so start with who decided that and when.
So the defense is that he just types really fast?
I didn't say a word about typing, Hale. I asked who entered that zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in. Answer that.
182 words in six minutes. Wow. Maybe he should be a court stenographer.
Leave my son's career out of it. "182 words in six minutes" from what document, on what date? Turn the screen and show me, or I'm going upstairs.
I'm not here as counsel, Hale, I'm here as his mother. You've given me a number with nothing behind it and two jokes, and I'm writing both of those down. Is there a document, or is that all you have?
